items.title: add native PS4 14.00 support
items.summary: ## Summary Adds PS4 firmware **14.00** as a first-class entry, the same way the existing 13.02-13.52 versions work: a real row in the offsets table, not an alias hack. ## What changed - **`js/ps4_offsets.js`** - new `PS4["14.00"]` row. Reuses the 13.52 WebKit gadgets and module offsets (14.00 ships the same WebKit), carries **no kernel addresses of its own**, and declares `own_kernel_stage: true`, `kpatch: "1400.bin"`, `payload: undefined`. Adds `own_kernel_stage` to `OPTIONAL_KEYS`. - **`js/afterglow.js`** (new) - the 14.00 kernel stage, ported from [`well0nez/afterglow-web`](https://github.com/well0nez/afterglow-web) (AGPL, attribution and provenance kept in the file header). It brings its own kernel primitives instead of reusing the 13.x chain. - **`js/jb.js`** - when a row sets `own_kernel_stage`, hand off to afterglow once the WebKit primitive, module bases and syscall stubs are up,
items.author: GamerReady

items.title: add native PS4 10.01-12.52 support (lapse + poops stages)
items.summary: Rows below 13.00 carry WebKit gadgets and syscall stubs but **not** the ten kernel RVAs `js/jb.js`'s chain reads, so that chain cannot run them — it soft-fails at `kernel-table-present` after looking supported. They are driven by two complete exploits instead, ported from [rawgame4](https://github.com/rawgame4/rawgame4.github.io/): | firmware | stage | file | |---|---|---| | 10.01 – 12.02 | lapse | `js/chain_lapse.js` | | 12.50 – 12.52 | poops | `js/chain_poops.js` | | 13.00 – 13.52 | this repo's chain | `js/jb.js` | | 14.00 | afterglow | `js/afterglow.js` | **13.00 deliberately does not hand off.** Its row already has the full kernel table and is proven through the aio chain this repo runs; routing it to poops would be a regression. Only rows that genuinely lack the kernel table move. ### The ordering constraint that shapes this The handoff runs **before** `jb.js` builds its primitive.

items.title: 14.00 (CUH-2016A, Belize): payload wedges console, no kexec handoff (v25.2)
items.summary: **Console:** PS4 Slim CUH-2016A (Belize), retail FW **14.00** **GoldHEN:** 2.4b18.13 **Loader:** v25.2 (2026-10-31) ### What happens Launching the Linux payload immediately: - HDMI loses signal - GoldHEN services die (FTP 2121, BinLoader 9090, klog 3232 all closed) - the console still answers ICMP, but there is no DHCP, no telnet, and no netconsole output - only a power cycle recovers; Orbis is unaffected afterwards Tested with: - `linux-1024mb.elf` run from GoldHEN's payloader - `linux-1024mb.bin` sent to GoldHEN's binloader on 9090 Same result both ways. With `netconsole=...` plus a static `ip=` in `bootargs.txt`, a listener on the LAN received **0 bytes**, so I do not think the kernel ever starts. This looks like a failed kexec handoff, the same symptom as #11 (13.52, Belize), where the resolution was to boot from a **USB drive** because internal `/data/linux/boot` was not being used.
